A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, references, and complete appendices. Content can be reliably matched across the substantial reformatting and relocation of material.

before.justification: V2 reports original synthetic online-allocation experiments, including linear and nonlinear utility functions, baseline comparisons, and sensitivity analyses in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds comparisons against efficiency-only and fairness-only allocation variants in Section 5, Figure 4.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 changes the stated UCB confidence multiplier by replacing tL²/λ with tL²/(λd). This changes the specified exploration bonus. Initialization, estimator updates, goodness-based allocation, Thompson sampling, and the nonlinear adaptation otherwise retain their procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic online allocation with linear and polynomial nonlinear utilities, including variations in item copies, agents, and feature dimensions. The nonlinear experiments highlighted in v3's main text already appeared in v2's Appendix D.

E2.justification: V3 Figure 4 adds OFD-Eff-UCB, OFD-Eff-TS, OFD-Fair-UCB, and OFD-Fair-TS alongside the retained Uniform and Greedy baselines. These provide a focused extension to alternative welfare objectives using the existing UCB/TS framework.

E3.justification: The added Figure 4 comparison uses linear configurations with d = 6, 10, 14, and 20, 10,000 items, 10 agents, and ρ = 0.85. Existing experiments retain their reported generation procedures, budgets, and metrics; relocated plots do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Figure 4 adds an objective-choice control: optimizing USW alone or ESW alone is compared with balancing fairness and efficiency. The earlier sensitivity analyses for copies, agent count, dimension, and ρ are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are repeated 20 times and report 95% confidence intervals. V3 introduces no different run-count, seed, significance-testing, or uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: V3 adds the Figure 4 results showing lower final regret for OFD-UCB/TS than the added welfare-specific controls across four linear configurations. All experimental plot images from v2 are retained unchanged, so their relocation introduces no revised numerical findings.

T1.justification: V3 revises Theorem 1's logarithmic factor from log(λ + TL/d) to log(1 + TL²/(λd)), adjusts confidence radii, and adds T > N qualifications. Appendix C revises monotonicity and rank-dependent weight arguments in Lemmas 3–4. Appendix E corrects coefficient bounds and strengthens log-Lipschitz assumptions to require separation from zero. Appendix B additionally defines oracle-history regret in Equation (3), leaving its additional term unbounded.

C1.justification: The central claims remain contextual-bandit allocation for numerous items with few copies, goodness-based fairness–efficiency balancing, conditional sublinear regret, and empirical validation. Renaming the retained Equation (1) quantity 'fair regret' does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix B explicitly distinguishes the existing policy-history benchmark from an oracle's own allocation history and acknowledges that bounding the latter's additional regret remains open. New FAQs also identify the absence of theoretical copy-count improvements and explain scalability and policy-dependent objective selection, materially clarifying applicability and limitations.

D1.justification: V3 adds a repository hyperlink and reports public code availability in the abstract. Appendix D removes v2's inconsistent explicit polynomial-feature expansion example while retaining the stated degree-two transformation and hardware information. The PDFs do not establish an actual preprocessing change.

R1.justification: V3 makes limited citation additions, including Clerici et al. (2024) and Schutz (1951), and removes several general bandit references. It corrects the fair-MAB description and explicitly relates fair regret to Sim et al. (2021), while retaining its principal positioning against existing online fair-division work.

P1.justification: V3 extensively edits prose and notation, organizes the introduction around three labeled challenges, and moves fair-MAB related work into Section 1.1. It promotes Appendix E.1 to Appendix F and adds FAQs, acknowledgements, and an impact statement, substantially revising the document's presentation and organization.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column proceedings layout. Existing experimental panels are extensively regrouped and moved between the main text and appendices, with revised captions and references; Figure 4 adds a new four-panel comparison.

improvement.justification: V3 improves precision through corrections to mathematical statements and assumptions, clarifies the oracle benchmark's limitations, and adds useful welfare-objective controls and code-access information. These provide a supported overall benefit, while most empirical evidence is retained and the stronger oracle-history analysis remains unfinished.
